name: stage-path
title: Stage path
description: A chevron path through stages (Lead, Qualified, Proposal, Won): done, current and next, clickable when you allow it.
docs: Pass stages (id, label, optional date and note) and current, the id of the stage the item is at. Without onStageChange it is a read-only record. With it, every stage you may go to is a button that calls onStageChange(id, from) before anything moves: change current yourself when you accept, and return a promise to have the stage shown as busy meanwhile. Going back to a finished stage needs allowBackward. lostLabel adds a terminal outcome (it calls onStageChange with the id "lost"), and lost draws the item as ended there, with current as the last stage it reached. When a press made with the keyboard or a pointer moves the item, focus follows it to the stage it is at (or the outcome), which is no longer a button, so the keyboard keeps its place; the arrow keys pass through that stage and Tab still goes from button to button. A screen reader hears an ordered list (Stage 3 of 5: Proposal, current) and, politely, what happened (Proposal, stage 3 of 5, or Closed lost at stage 3 of 5; every sentence can be reworded through labels); in a box under 28rem only the current stage keeps its name and the others shrink to a check or a number.
